[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.8] (7) Where the creditor, or any other claimant to the goods subject to enforcement to whom notice of claim to exempt goods was given, fails, within the period mentioned in paragraph (3), to give the required notice, the enforcement agent or relevant enforcement officer may seek—

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.8] (a) the directions of the court by way of an application; and

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.8] (b) an order preventing the bringing of any claim against them for, or in respect of, their having taken control of or seized by execution any of the goods or their having failed to do so. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.8] (8) An application under paragraph (7) must be made to the court which issued the writ or warrant conferring power to take control of controlled goods, or the writ of execution or, if the power to take control of controlled goods was conferred under an enactment, to the County Court hearing centre which is the debtor’s home court. ## Procedure for making a claim to exempt goods where the claim is disputed

## 85.9

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (1) Where a creditor, or any other claimant to goods subject to enforcement to whom notice of a claim to exempt goods was given, gives notice under rule 85.8 that the claim to exempt goods, or any part of it, is disputed, and wishes to maintain their claim on the goods subject to enforcement, the following procedure will apply. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (2) The debtor must make an application within 7 days of receiving the notice under rule 85.8(3) which must be supported by—

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (a) a witness statement—

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (i) describing any goods to which a claim to exempt goods is made; and

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (ii) setting out the grounds upon which such claim is based; and

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (b) copies of any supporting documents that will assist the court to determine such claim. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (3) In the High Court the debtor must serve the application notice and supporting witness statements and exhibits on—

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (a) the creditor;

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (b) any other claimant to the goods subject to enforcement of whom they are aware; and

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (c) the enforcement agent or relevant enforcement officer. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (4) In the County Court the debtor must provide to the court when the application is made the addresses for service of—

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (a) the creditor;

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (b) any other claimant to controlled goods of whom the debtor is aware; and

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (c) the enforcement agent,

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (‘the respondents’), and the court will serve the application notice and supporting witness statements and exhibits on the respondents. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (5) An application under paragraph (2) must be made to the court which issued the writ or warrant conferring power to take control of controlled goods or the writ of execution or if the power to take control of controlled goods was conferred under an enactment, to the debtor’s home court. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (6) The application notice will be referred to a Master or District Judge. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (7) On receipt of an application for a claim to exempt goods, the Master or District Judge may—

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (a) give directions for further evidence;

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (b) list a hearing to give directions;

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (c) list a hearing of the application;

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (d) make directions for the retention, sale or disposal of the goods subject to the claim to exempt goods;

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.9] (e) give directions for determination of any issue raised by the exempt goods claim. ## SECTION VI POWERS OF THE COURT HEARING ANY APPLICATION UNDER THIS PART

## Directions and determination of claims

## 85.10

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (1) At any hearing of any application under this Part the court may—

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (a) determine an application summarily; or

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (b) give directions for the determination of any issue raised by such application;

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (c) order that any issue between any parties to a claim to goods subject to enforcement be stated and tried, and give all necessary directions for trial;

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (d) give directions for the purpose of determining the amount of the required payments or any underpayment of the required payments pursuant to paragraph 60(5) of Schedule 12 and regulation 49 of the TCG Regulations;

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (e) summarily determine the amount of the required payments or any underpayment of the required payments pursuant to paragraph 60(5) of Schedule 12 9 and regulation 49 of the TCG Regulations 10 ;

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (f) make directions for the retention, sale or disposal of goods subject to enforcement and for the payment of any proceeds of sale; or

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (g) make any order that the court considers appropriate. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (2) Where a claimant to goods subject to enforcement or a debtor making a claim to exempt goods does not appear at any hearing listed on the application or, having appeared, fails or refuses to comply with an order made in the proceedings, the court may make an order declaring such claimant, or the debtor, and all persons claiming under them, for ever barred from prosecuting their claim against the creditor or any other claimant to the goods subject to enforcement, but such an order will not affect the rights of any other claimants to the goods subject to enforcement as between themselves. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (3) Where a claimant to goods subject to enforcement alleges that they are entitled, under a bill of sale or otherwise, to the controlled goods or to the executed goods by way of security for debt, the court may order those goods or any part thereof to be sold and may direct that the proceeds of sale be applied in such manner and on such terms as may be just and as may be specified in the order. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.10] (4) Nothing in this rule limits the court’s case management powers to make any other directions permissible under these Rules. ## Trial of issue

## 85.11

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.11] (1) Part 39 will, with the necessary modifications, apply to the trial of an issue in an application under this Part as it applies to the trial of a claim. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.11] (2) The court by which an issue is tried may give such judgment or make such order as finally to dispose of all questions arising in the application. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.11] (3) Practice Direction 2B applies to the trial of an issue in an application under this Part. ## Costs

## 85.12

[PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.12] (1) The court may in or for the purposes of any application under this Part make such order as to costs as it thinks just. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.12] (2) Where a claimant to goods subject to enforcement or a debtor in a claim to exempt goods fails to appear at a hearing, the court may direct that the enforcement agent’s or officer’s costs and creditor’s costs will be assessed by a Master, District Judge, Costs judge or Costs officer. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.12] (3) In a claim to controlled goods a debtor may request the court to assess the costs incurred by an enforcement agent, in which case the court will apply the Taking Control of Goods (Fees) Regulations 2014 11 to such assessment. [PART 85 – CLAIMS ON CONTROLLED GOODS AND EXECUTED GOODS > 85.12] (4) In a claim to executed goods a debtor may request the court to assess the costs incurred by an enforcement officer, in which case the court will apply Schedule 3 of the High Court Enforcement Officers Regulations 2004 12 to such assessment, save in relation to the costs of execution of writs of sequestration and writs relating to ecclesiastical property. ## Footnotes
